rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir frames the passage as a reminder of God choosing and speaking privately to Moses, giving him striking signs, and sending him to Pharaoh's elite, who rejected them arrogantly.
rows.anchor: مذكرا له ما كان من أمر موسى، كيف اصطفاه الله وكلمه، وناجاه وأعطاه من الآيات العظيمة الباهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was traveling with his family, lost the way during a dark night, and saw a fire from the side of the Mount.
rows.anchor: أي: اذكر حين سار موسى بأهله، فأضل الطريق، وذلك في ليل وظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb describes Moses seeing a blazing, flaring fire.
rows.anchor: رأى نارا تأجج (2) وتضطرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hoped to learn the route or bring back a firebrand so his family could warm themselves.
rows.anchor: أي: عن الطريق، {أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون} أي: تتدفؤون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His prediction came true: he returned with momentous news and took from the fire a great light.
rows.anchor: وكان كما قال، فإنه رجع منها بخبر عظيم، واقتبس منها نورا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the site Moses saw a tremendous sight: fire flared in a green tree without consuming its greenery, and its light reached the sky.
rows.anchor: والنار تضطرم في شجرة خضراء، لا تزداد النار إلا توقدا، ولا تزداد الشجرة إلا خضرة ونضرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others report that what Moses saw was not fire but a glowing light.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: لم تكن نارا، إنما كانت نورا (4) يتوهج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the light as the light of the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس: نور رب العالمين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the blessing as sanctification.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: [أي] (5) قدس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, Said ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, and Qatada say those around the fire were angels.
rows.anchor: {ومن حولها} أي: من الملائكة. قاله ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، والحسن، وقتادة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports that the Prophet said God does not sleep, controls the balance, and receives the deeds of night and day in turn.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله لا ينام، ولا ينبغي له أن ينام

rows.speaker: المسعودي
rows.claim: Al-Masudi adds that God's veil is light or fire; if uncovered, the radiance of His face would burn everything His sight reaches.
rows.anchor: زاد المسعودي: "وحجابه النور -أو النار -لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه

words: بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا
rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda recited this verse after the report; Ibn Kathir says its underlying hadith is recorded in Sahih Muslim from Amr ibn Murra.
rows.anchor: ثم قرأ أبو عبيدة: {أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها}

words: بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that the underlying report is also transmitted in Sahih Muslim through Amr ibn Murra.
rows.anchor: وأصل هذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيح لمسلم، من حديث عمرو بن مرة، به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts as He wills, resembles no creature, is not encompassed by His creations, and is exalted, unique, self-sufficient, and unlike created things; neither earth nor heavens contain Him.
rows.anchor: ولا يشبه شيئا من مخلوقاته، ولا يحيط به شيء من مصنوعاته، وهو العلي العظيم، المباين لجميع المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told that his interlocutor is God, invincible and overpowering all things, and wise in His actions and words.
rows.anchor: أعلمه (2) أن الذي يخاطبه ويناجيه هو ربه الله العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands Moses to drop his staff as a clear proof that God freely chooses and has power over everything.
rows.anchor: ثم أمره أن يلقي عصاه من يده؛ ليظهر له دليلا واضحا على أنه الفاعل المختار، القادر على كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff immediately became an enormous, terrifying serpent that moved with great speed.
rows.anchor: انقلبت في الحال حية عظيمة هائلة في غاية الكبر، وسرعة الحركة مع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jann is a kind of snake distinguished by especially fast, restless movement; Ibn Kathir notes a hadith prohibiting killing house snakes.
rows.anchor: والجان: ضرب من الحيات، أسرعه حركة، وأكثره اضطرابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses ran away without looking back because he was intensely frightened.
rows.anchor: أي: لم يلتفت من شدة فرقه

words: لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses not to fear what he sees because God intends to choose him as a messenger and make him an honored prophet.
rows.anchor: فإني أريد أن أصطفيك رسولا وأجعلك نبيا وجيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reading Solomon's letter, the queen consults her elite about what has befallen her and says she will not decide until they attend and advise.
rows.anchor: لما قرأت عليهم كتاب سليمان استشارتهم في أمرها، وما قد نزل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her advisers boast of their numbers, equipment, and strength, then leave the decision to her and promise obedience.
rows.anchor: منوا إليها بعددهم وعددهم وقوتهم، ثم فوضوا إليها بعد ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri criticizes the men for handing rule to a woman and says she proved more prudent and better informed about Solomon's forces.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن البصري، رحمه الله: فوضوا أمرهم إلى علجة تضطرب ثدياها، فلما قالوا لها ما قالوا، كانت هي أحزم رأيا منهم

words: إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا۟ قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen feared that resisting Solomon would bring his armies, including jinn, humans, and birds, and cause their ruin and destruction.
rows.anchor: وما سخر له من الجن والإنس والطير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that kings who seize a country destroy it and humiliate its rulers and soldiers by killing or captivity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي إذا دخلوا بلدا (1) عنوة أفسدوه، أي: خربوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the queen's statement about kings is affirmed by God with the words, They do likewise.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قالت بلقيس: {إن الملوك إذا دخلوا قرية أفسدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen shifts to a truce and tactical appeasement, sending an appropriate gift to test Solomon; she hopes he may accept it, demand annual tribute, and spare them war.
rows.anchor: ثم عدلت إلى المهادنة والمصالحة والمسالمة والمخادعة والمصانعة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada praises the queen's good judgment both before and after accepting Islam, noting that she knew gifts influence people.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: رحمها الله ورضي عنها، ما كان أعقلها في إسلامها وفي شركها!! علمت أن الهدية تقع موقعا من الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغير واحد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others report that the queen told her people: if Solomon accepts the gift, he is a king to fight; if he refuses it, he is a prophet to follow.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغير واحد: قالت لقومها: إن قبل الهدية فهو ملك فقاتلوه، وإن لم يقبلها فهو نبي فاتبعوه

rows.speaker: غير واحد من المفسرين، من السلف وغيرهم
rows.claim: Several early and later commentators say the queen sent a great gift of gold, jewels, pearls, and other valuables.
rows.anchor: ذكر غير واحد من المفسرين، من السلف وغيرهم: أنها بعثت إليه بهدية عظيمة من ذهب وجواهر ولآلئ

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reports specify that she sent a brick of gold.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أرسلت بلبنة من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir considers the report that the queen sent golden vessels to be the sound view.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنها أرسلت [إليه] (1) بآنية من ذهب

rows.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وغيرهما
rows.claim: Mujahid, Said ibn Jubayr, and others say the queen sent girls dressed as boys and boys dressed as girls, testing whether Solomon could identify them as a prophet.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وغيرهما: وأرسلت جواري في زي الغلمان، وغلمان في زي الجواري، وقالت: إن عرف هؤلاء من هؤلاء فهو نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Solomon had the disguised youths perform ablution: the girl poured water over her hand while the boy scooped it, allowing him to tell them apart.
rows.anchor: فجعلت الجارية تفرغ على يدها من الماء، وجعل الغلام يغترف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another version says the girl washed the inside of her hand before its back, while the boy did the reverse.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل جعلت الجارية تغسل باطن (3) يدها قبل ظاهرها، والغلام بالعكس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further version says the girls washed from their palms toward their elbows, and the boys from elbows toward palms.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل جعلت الجواري يغتسلن (4) من أكفهن إلى مرافقهن، والغلمان من مرافقهم إلى أكفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir sees no contradiction among these different descriptions of how Solomon distinguished the disguised girls and boys.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة بين ذلك كله، والله أعلم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the gift included a cup to be filled with pure water from neither sky nor earth, and a bead and thread to test Solomon; he ran horses until they sweated, filled the cup with their sweat, and threaded the bead. Ibn Kathir says this is uncertain and mostly Israelite lore.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم: أنها أرسلت إليه بقدح ليملأه ماء رواء، لا من السماء ولا من الأرض، فأجرى الخيل حتى عرقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon ignores the gift and rebukes them for trying to bribe him to let them keep their rule and shirk; God's gifts of kingdom, wealth, and troops are better, and he wants only Islam or the sword.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن سليمان، عليه السلام، لم ينظر إلى ما جاءوا به بالكلية، ولا اعتنى به، بل أعرض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon says the envoys are the ones who delight in gifts and treasures, unlike him.
rows.anchor: وأما أنا فلا أقبل منكم إلا الإسلام أو السيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Solomon ordered the devils to adorn a thousand palaces with gold and silver; the queen's envoys then wondered what use he had for their gift.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، رضي الله عنه: أمر سليمان الشياطين فموهوا له ألف قصر من ذهب وفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir infers that rulers may prepare and display their grandeur to visiting envoys and emissaries.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على جواز تهيؤ الملوك وإظهارهم الزينة للرسل والقصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon orders the envoys to return with their gift.
rows.anchor: {ارجع إليهم} أي: بهديتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their people would have no ability to fight Solomon's forces.
rows.anchor: أي: لا طاقة لهم بقتالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would be driven from their land humiliated and subdued.
rows.anchor: {ولنخرجنهم منها} أي: من بلدهم، {أذلة وهم صاغرون} أي: مهانون مدحورون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the envoys returned and reported Solomon's response, the queen and her people submitted and traveled to him humbly, intending to embrace Islam; Solomon was pleased at their arrival.
rows.anchor: سمعت وأطاعت هي وقومها، وأقبلت تسير إليه في جنودها خاضعة ذليلة، معظمة لسليمان، ناوية متابعته في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Copts feared that killing Israelite boys would eventually leave them without laborers for their arduous work, so they warned Pharaoh that the elders would die and women could not replace men.
rows.anchor: إنه يوشك -إن استمر هذا الحال -أن يموت شيوخهم، وغلمانهم لا يعيشون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh ordered newborn boys killed in alternating years; Aaron was born in a spared year, while Moses was born in a killing year.
rows.anchor: فأمر بقتل الولدان عاما وتركهم عاما، فولد هارون، عليه السلام، في السنة التي يتركون فيها الولدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh appointed watchers and midwives to register pregnancies and inspect births; Coptic women alone attended Israelite mothers at delivery.
rows.anchor: وكان لفرعون أناس موكلون بذلك، وقوابل يدرن على النساء، فمن رأينها قد حملت أحصوا اسمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a woman gave birth to a girl, the attendants left her; if she bore a boy, armed executioners entered and killed him.
rows.anchor: فإذا ولدت المرأة جارية تركنها وذهبن، وإن ولدت غلاما دخل أولئك الذباحون، بأيديهم الشفار المرهفة، فقتلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' pregnancy showed no usual signs and escaped the midwives' notice; after his birth his mother feared for and dearly loved him, and people who saw him loved him too. Ibn Kathir links this to God placing love on him.
rows.anchor: لم يظهر عليها مخايل الحمل كغيرها، ولم تفطن لها الدايات، ولكن لما وضعته ذكرا ضاقت به ذرعا، وخافت عليه خوفا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired Moses' mother privately to nurse him and, when afraid, place him in the river without fear or grief, promising to return him and make him a messenger.
rows.anchor: ألهمت في سرها، وألقي في خلدها، ونفث في روعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' mother's house stood on the Nile; she made a basket, prepared it, nursed him, and hid him in it when someone she feared entered, keeping it tethered by a cord.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه كانت دارها على حافة النيل، فاتخذت تابوتا، ومهدت فيه مهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One day she put Moses in the basket when a feared visitor arrived, forgot to tie it, and the river carried it to Pharaoh's house.
rows.anchor: وأرسلته في البحر وذهلت عن أن تربطه، فذهب مع الماء واحتمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's maidservants found the basket and brought it to his wife without knowing its contents; she opened it, saw a beautiful boy, and God placed love for him in her heart, to her good fortune and her husband's ruin.
rows.anchor: فالتقطه الجواري فاحتملنه، فذهبن به إلى امرأة فرعون، ولا يدرين ما فيه

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others take the lām as indicating an eventual consequence, not the family's purpose, since they did not intend to capture someone who would become their enemy and grief.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording appears to support Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Kathir prefers a purposive lām in light of the context: God caused them to take Moses so he would become their enemy and grief, more fully defeating their precautions.
rows.anchor: ولكن إذا نظر إلى معنى السياق فإنه تبقى (5) اللام للتعليل

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: In a letter to Qadariyya denying scripture and God's decrees, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz argues that God's prior knowledge made Moses Pharaoh's enemy and grief, citing the promise to show Pharaoh what he feared and rejecting the claim that Pharaoh might have chosen to support Moses.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن أمير المؤمنين عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه كتب كتابا إلى قوم من القدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After killing the Copt, Moses spent the morning afraid of the consequences, looking around and anticipating what would happen.
rows.anchor: مخبرا عن موسى، عليه السلام (3) ، لما قتل ذلك القبطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a road Moses again encountered the Israelite who had sought his help the previous day, now fighting another man and calling to him for aid.
rows.anchor: الذي استنصره بالأمس على ذلك القبطي يقاتل آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls the Israelite manifestly misguided and persistently troublesome.
rows.anchor: أي: ظاهر الغواية كثير الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses resolved to strike the Copt, the fearful, weak Israelite thought Moses meant to attack him and blurted out the murder from the day before, protesting that Moses wanted to be a tyrant rather than a reformer.
rows.anchor: ثم عزم على البطش بذلك القبطي، فاعتقد الإسرائيلي لخوره وضعفه وذلته أن موسى إنما يريد قصده لما سمعه يقول ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only Moses and the Israelite knew about the earlier killing; the Copt overheard the Israelite's words, reported them at Pharaoh's gate, and provoked Pharaoh to seek Moses' death.
rows.anchor: فلما سمعها ذلك القبطي لقفها من فمه، ثم ذهب بها إلى باب فرعون فألقاها عنده، فعلم بذلك

words: وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌۭ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man took a different, shorter route than Pharaoh's messengers and reached Moses first, which is why the verse describes him as a man of action.
rows.anchor: وصفه بالرجولية لأنه خالف الطريق، فسلك طريقا أقرب من طريق الذين بعثوا وراءه، فسبق إلى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elite are conferring together about Moses and intend to kill him.
rows.anchor: {إن الملأ يأتمرون بك} أي: يتشاورون فيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man urges Moses to leave the city and assures him that his warning is sincere.
rows.anchor: {ليقتلوك فاخرج} أي: من البلد {إني لك من الناصحين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On learning of Pharaoh's plot, Moses left Egypt alone, unused to a life of flight after comfort, luxury, and status; he looked around fearfully.
rows.anchor: خرج من مصر وحده، ولم يألف ذلك قلبه، بل كان في رفاهية ونعمة ورئاسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to save him from Pharaoh and his elite, whom Ibn Kathir identifies as the unjust people.
rows.anchor: أي: من فرعون وملئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses took a well-traveled route toward Midian, hoped God would guide him to the right way, and God guided him in this life and the next, making him a guide who was himself guided.
rows.anchor: أخذ طريقا سالكا مهيعا فرح بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Midian's well, Moses saw a crowd watering sheep and two women holding their flock back to avoid harm; they waited for the shepherds to finish because their father was elderly.
rows.anchor: وكان لها بئر ترده رعاء الشاء

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar reports that ten men alone could lift the stone covering Midian's well; Moses lifted it and drew one bucketful until the sheep were watered. Ibn Kathir grades the chain sound.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، أن موسى

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's claim to divinity expresses his disbelief, tyranny, and false pretension; he demanded that his people acknowledge him as a god, and they obeyed foolishly.
rows.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن كفر فرعون وطغيانه وافترائه في دعوى الإلهية لنفسه القبيحة

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir links Pharaoh's public claim to his gathering and declaring himself the highest lord, which his people accepted, and God's making him a warning for later people.
rows.anchor: {فحشر فنادى * فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh had also threatened to imprison Moses if he worshipped a god other than Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh orders his minister, administrator, and state adviser Haman to fire clay into bricks for construction.
rows.anchor: أمر وزيره هامان ومدبر رعيته ومشير دولته أن يوقد له على الطين، ليتخذ له آجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣarḥ is a lofty, towering palace; another verse describes Pharaoh demanding a tower to reach the paths of the heavens.
rows.anchor: وهو القصر المنيف الرفيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh built the tallest structure the world had seen to make his subjects think Moses' claim of a god besides Pharaoh was false.
rows.anchor: إنما أراد بهذا أن يظهر لرعيته تكذيب موسى فيما زعمه

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir's view, adopted here, is that Pharaoh called Moses a liar for claiming a god existed besides Pharaoh, not for claiming God had sent him; Pharaoh denied a creator, as shown by his questions and threats.
rows.anchor: فإنه قال: {وما رب العالمين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day God rebukes and threatens the polytheists, asking where the idols and rivals they worshipped can be and whether they will help or defend them.
rows.anchor: يعني: أين الآلهة التي كنتم تعبدونها في الدار الدنيا، من الأصنام والأنداد، هل ينصرونكم أو ينتصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those upon whom the decree has fallen are devils, rebellious beings, and callers to disbelief; they admit misleading their followers but disavow being worshipped.
rows.anchor: يعني: من الشياطين والمردة والدعاة إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites other verses where false gods disown worshippers, become their enemies, and are cursed by their followers on seeing the punishment.
rows.anchor: فشهدوا عليهم أنهم أغووهم فاتبعوهم، ثم تبرؤوا من عبادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to call their partners to rescue them as they had hoped in worldly life; the partners do not answer, and the people realize they are bound for Hell.
rows.anchor: ليخلصوكم مما أنتم فيه، كما كنتم ترجون منهم في الدار الدنيا
